TL;DR: Now you can play around with the Machine Learning Knowledge Graph Explorer [ https://substack.com/redirect/87a2f968-ff94-4cc1-a748-a2fece453ac3?j=eyJ1IjoiOG81NG4ifQ.6oeetudtJEh-zO1onUJvtadWEdbodFIw0h4xbugrh1o ] I’ve been building. Check it out; it’s awesome.
Hey!
I spent my last week building the knowledge graph of machine learning, mapping out every concept and its relations.
With this, you can visualize subfields, the roots of machine learning (surprise: mathematics), the central concepts, and a bunch of other cool stuff, like tracing the prerequisites (yellow edges) and dependents (blue edges) of gradient descent.
Now you can explore them yourself with a little app I built Codex and Claude built. The app is publicly hosted on GitHub pages at https://the-palindrome.github.io/ml-knowledge-graph/ [ https://substack.com/redirect/87a2f968-ff94-4cc1-a748-a2fece453ac3?j=eyJ1IjoiOG81NG4ifQ.6oeetudtJEh-zO1onUJvtadWEdbodFIw0h4xbugrh1o ], but you can check the source at https://github.com/the-palindrome/ml-knowledge-graph [ https://substack.com/redirect/34a321cb-8963-4df2-b205-3be6f330979a?j=eyJ1IjoiOG81NG4ifQ.6oeetudtJEh-zO1onUJvtadWEdbodFIw0h4xbugrh1o ] as well.
